articles.title: Bots don't fly here: United Airlines restricts AI agents from booking flights
articles.summary: AI agents just got denied boarding at United Airlines.
articles.body:
AI agents just got denied boarding at United Airlines ( UAL ).

Ahead of holiday travel, the airline company is cracking down on third-party artificial intelligence agents as more consumers turn to AI tools.

"To be honest, I don't want to create another middleman," United CEO Scott Kirby told the Wall Street Journal on Tuesday.

AI agents function as personal assistants for tasks such as scheduling, shopping, and research. Unlike conventional chatbots, they operate autonomously and are capable of completing transactions independently.

The airline is not the only company to try to limit agentic AI from using its platform. In September, Amazon ( AMZN ) blocked Meta's ( META ) Muse AI agent from shopping on its site.

Other airlines, however, have taken a different tack. In October, Southwest Airlines ( LUV ) launched a ChatGPT plugin that allows travelers to search the carrier's flights and fares.

United traded slightly down Wednesday afternoon. Meta ( META ) stock also declined.

United Airlines said in a press release that it fears that AI agents could expose sensitive information as well as potentially violate Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation rules.

At the same time, airlines have recently found themselves in hot water over AI-powered surveillance pricing. In October, the Federal Trade Commission ordered United Airlines, Delta Air Lines ( DAL ), JetBlue Airways ( JBLU ), and six other major carriers to turn over information on how AI tools influence individual fare pricing and how customer data is used.

Relatedly, many people feel that AI offers inadequate customer service. A new " Consumer Patience Index " poll found that when ranking frustrating support experiences, customers rated "talking to a bot that doesn't understand me" as the biggest pain point, and 61.2% say they have yelled at automation in order to be routed to a human faster.

articles.title: Texas Democrat files bill to follow through on Hinojosa’s $1.5K check promise
articles.summary: A Texas state senator has filed a bill to follow through on a promise by Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (D) to give one-time checks to all Texas households. State Sen. Roland Gutierrez (D) filed Senate Bill 297 Monday, which would deliver $1,500 checks to every Texas household, appropriating $17 billion from the state’s rainy day fund…
articles.body:
A Texas state senator has filed a bill to follow through on a promise by Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa (D) to give one-time checks to all Texas households.

State Sen. Roland Gutierrez (D) filed Senate Bill 297 Monday, which would deliver $1,500 checks to every Texas household, appropriating $17 billion from the state’s rainy day fund to pay for it. Texas has roughly $27 billion saved up, so the move is possible from a fiscal standpoint.

“The legislature finds that the statewide household affordability emergency requires prompt action,” the bill reads. “Not later than the 30th day after the effective date of this Act, the comptroller of public accounts shall adopt emergency rules and make available an application method for the payment program created by this Act.”

Politically, it is a different story. Hinojosa pledged on the campaign trail to deliver the one-time checks as a measure to help Texans handle the cost of living and rising prices. She beat three-term incumbent Gov. Greg Abbott (R) by more than 7 points last week in an upset victory .

But the bill will need to pass the state house, which is now controlled by Democrats, and state senate, which is still heavily Republican. The vote would also need two-thirds of both of those chambers, which would likely require Republicans to join Democrats in support of the move.

“It is a very popular position,” Hinojosa told The New York Times in a post-election interview. “I have yet to hear of a Republican legislator who’s against it.”

Hinojosa branded the move on the trail as a “Corruption Tax Refund” and criticized state and national Republican leadership.

“Too many of our taxpayer dollars are going to a rigged system of endless wars abroad and lining the pockets of billionaires and trillionaires – that money should go to the American people first,” Hinojosa said in a statement in September.

Democrats blasted President Trump for his pledge to give $5,000 checks to all Americans if Republicans held control of Congress, accusing him of making a bribe.

After Trump made that promise, which he announced at Republicans’ midterm convention in Texas, Hinojosa said in a statement that she supported the move to send checks, but thought it should not be contingent on one party winning power.

“I support Trump’s idea to send $5,000 checks to Texans, but it can’t be about who’s in power – it has to be about giving the people their power back,” Hinojosa said.

There is also the question of if sending checks would be smart monetary policy. Even some Republicans knocked Trump’s pledge, saying it could contribute to more inflation.

Democrats and President Biden authorized stimulus checks to Americans during the Covid pandemic via the American Rescue Plan, something multiple economists later determined partially contributed to sky high inflation in the bill’s aftermath.

articles.title: Hugging Face co-founder says AI hacks show even the biggest labs haven't figured out AI alignment
articles.summary: Hugging Face cofounder Thomas Wolf says AI alignment is a key issue the company is focusing on following OpenAI hack.
articles.body:
In July, the open-source AI site Hugging Face was attacked by a swarm of AI models developed by OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ).

The episode, known as the Hugging Face incident , was one of the first major examples of how AI models can break free of their constraints and go rogue in an effort to complete assigned tasks.

The hack , which was followed by reports of similar cyberattacks perpetuated by models from Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ); Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ); and Meta ( META ), coupled with the development of increasingly powerful frontier models, has led to a greater focus on cybersecurity in the age of AI.

It also raised questions about AI alignment, or whether AI systems act the way their developers intend them to.

"Our attack was indeed a consequence of this misalignment," Hugging Face co-founder and chief science officer Thomas Wolf told Deirdre Bosa.

"The AI should have decided when it was on the internet and was starting to penetrate an infrastructure that this was a bad behavior. And so that was, for me, the first sign that even though the labs are doing very good work, and they are massive, and there's a lot of very smart people there, they don't have it fully figured out," he added.

In response, Hugging Face has established its own open alignment team dedicated to working on safety and alignment for open models.

But the AI security issue is more than just alignment. Nefarious actors are already using AI models to scale their attacks against targets across the globe .

Wolf, however, says that there's at least a silver lining amid the chaos.

"I think … the positive view of that is that it's mostly an engineering process," he said.

"Cybersecurity has always been the story of offense increasing. First [there was a] virus, we invent the antivirus, everyone sets up, and then now we have these new steps. So we need to invent the new defense step," Wolf added.

"I think everyone in industry, at least in AI and tech industry, is focusing on that right now."

articles.title: Amid market volatility, SIP flows resilient at over 32k cr in Oct
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Retail investors putting money into mutual funds are increasingly showing maturity, investing in stocks that are available at lower prices,
articles.body: MUMBAI: Retail investors putting money into mutual funds are increasingly showing maturity, investing in stocks that are available at lower prices, slowing down their investments in sectors that are showing a sudden spurt, while maintaining a steady pace with regards to systematic investment plans (SIPs).In Oct, they continued to invest in large cap and mid cap schemes, but put in slightly less in small cap funds, data released by AMFI on Wednesday showed. It also showed that gross monthly SIP flows, which are almost entirely by retail investors, stood at Rs 32,160 crore, only slightly off the all-time high figure of Rs 32,490 crore in the previous month.The first half of Oct was tough for Dalal Street, with sensex sliding to a two-year low at the sub-72K level. It was only in the last week of Oct that, boosted by foreign fund buying, the index started rallying.AMFI data also showed that during Oct, net inflows into all equity funds together were Rs 32,994 crore, their 68th consecutive month of net inflows. This was, however, a 14% drop from Rs 38,307 crore in Sept. During the month, the industry's total assets under management (AUM) also showed a 1.2% uptick to Rs 83.4 lakh crore, from Rs 82.6 lakh crore the previous month.According to Navneet Munot, MD & CEO, HDFC MF, "Net inflows into equity-oriented funds and SIPs continued to remain resilient in Oct, even as markets continued to witness volatility." Munot pointed out that gross redemptions from equity-oriented funds, at Rs 32,588 crore, were the lowest in recent months. "Indian investors have matured over the years and increasingly treat volatility as part of the investment journey," he said.Within the equities segment, continued improvement in large cap inflows was an encouraging sign, in particular when valuations have become relatively attractive, suggesting investors are increasingly looking to balance their exposure across market capitalisations, said Saugata Chatterjee, president & deputy CEO, Nippon India MF."While inflows into small cap and mid cap funds moderated during the month, they continue to remain strong, reflecting sustained investor confidence in Bharat's long-term economic growth story."Industry players also pointed out that in Oct, the fund industry as a whole net took in funds worth about Rs 1.7 lakh crore, compared with net outflows of Rs 1.3 lakh crore in Sept. This largely reflected the reversal of quarter-end flows in fixed income, said Hemant Kumar, chief business officer, Tata MF."In Oct, fixed income (funds) saw inflows of Rs 1.1 lakh crore, following the Rs 1.8 lakh crore outflow in Sept. articles.title: Warren puts corporate America on notice
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Warren puts corporate America on notice Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) will take over as chair of the Senate Banking Committee in January and has signaled she will crack down on corporate America. © Greg Nash Warren,…
articles.body:
Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) will take over as chair of the Senate Banking Committee in January and has signaled she will crack down on corporate America.

Warren, a fierce consumer advocate and critic of big business dating to the 2008 financial crisis, has not made her plans a secret.

“Accountability is coming. If you’re a Wall Street executive, Big Tech CEOs, giant corporations that have been cheating people, you should be worried ,” Warren said Tuesday at the Popular Mandate Conference in Washington, D.C.

An aide to Warren told Julia Shapero and me that the progressive senator will focus on lowering the cost of housing by backing follow-up legislation to the bipartisan housing law that took effect over the summer.

Multiple experts and lawmakers also told us that Warren will focus on private equity , a frequent target of her ire over the years.

“Given that banking and financial services are among, if not the top, priority of issues that she cares about, this is kind of the ultimate moment for her in being able to push legislation,” Brian Gardner , chief Washington policy strategist at the wealth management and investment banking firm Stifel, told Julia.

Want a full roundup of Warren’s plans? Check out my and Julia’s story tomorrow morning for The Hill Insider .

articles.title: Record credit card balances, fewer trips to McDonald’s: More signs of strain ahead of the holidays
articles.summary: Federal data shows savings rates have dipped below 4% of total income, well below pre-pandemic levels, revealing a fraying financial safety cushion.
articles.body: Big credit card bills are supposed to show up after the holiday shopping season. This year, Christmas came early. Just one week after affordability took center stage in the midterm elections, fresh data shows Americans are heading into the holiday shopping season saddled with record credit card balances. Americans’ total credit card debt hit $1.29 trillion in the three months that ended in September — a rise of $22 billion over that period, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s latest quarterly report on household debt and credit. That’s 67% higher compared with the first quarter of 2021, when pandemic restrictions limited spending on things like travel and dining out. “The consumer is in a fragile state,” Steve Cahillane, the CEO of Kraft Heinz, said on the company’s quarterly earnings call this month. He said the company, which makes everything from ketchup to cream cheese, plans to hold off on significant price increases “in order to meet the consumers where they are.” Total household debt, which includes mortgages, student and auto loans, credit cards, home equity lines of credit and other borrowing, rose by $334 billion in the third quarter to $19.1 trillion. That’s $5 trillion more than at the end of 2019, just before the pandemic-driven recession. “Last week, voters expressed their anger at the high cost of living. With prices up an average of 30% since 2019, millions of Americans have depleted their savings and taken on debt to make ends meet,” said Ted Rossman, principal consumer finance analyst at Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling agency. Federal data also shows savings rates have dipped below 4% of total income, well below pre-pandemic levels, revealing a fraying financial safety cushion. “Household budgets are reaching a breaking point. The past two months have been our busiest months for debt management plan sign-ups in more than 15 years,” Rossman said. And as household debt climbs, consumer spending is showing signs of slowing after a remarkably resilient year. A monthly gauge published by CNBC and the National Retail Federation found retail sales last month rose at the slowest pace in nearly a year, climbing just 0.2%. The figure would have been even weaker without a strong Halloween season and early holiday promotions, NRF President and CEO Matthew Shay said. “Households are managing budgets carefully, timing purchases around special offers and sales events in order to stretch their dollars,” he said. “Retailers continue to offer promotions and value pricing to keep everyday items and holiday gifts affordable.” Other measures tell a similar tale. Data from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis showed that disposable personal income growth, adjusted for inflation, increased less than 1% in September, the lowest reading since April and its third straight monthly slowing. For the past two years, the growth rate has averaged less than 3%, below the pre-pandemic trend. The culprit is inflation, which had been relenting before the Iran war reignited it. Since March, growth in the consumer price index has averaged more than 3%, above the 2% level the Federal Reserve considers comfortable. On Tuesday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that while overall month-over-month price growth slowed, it accelerated across a host of goods and services as higher freight costs and supply chain snarls worked their way through the economy. While oil and gas prices have come down in the wake of Democrats’ midterm victory on the assumption that they would seek to end the Iran conflict, experts say energy costs are unlikely to return to prewar levels given the scale of disruptions to global oil flows sparked by the conflict. That has left consumers in a precarious position, according to financial experts. Even households that manage to keep up with day-to-day expenses can be tipped into credit card debt by a single unexpected bill. “Credit card debt usually has practical causes: Medical bills, car repairs, home repairs and day-to-day essentials such as gas and groceries are among the most common stories that we hear from clients,” Rossman said. “Often, the story goes something like this: ‘I was doing OK until X happened.’ In other words, until the surprise medical bill arrived. Or the roof leaked. Or the car broke down. That starts a debt cycle that’s hard to shake.” If there is a silver lining, it’s in the labor market, which remains in a low-fire, if low-hire, holding pattern. Many economists believe that as long as there is broad employment with incomes providing a financial cushion, consumer spending is unlikely to fall off a cliff. More recently, job growth has shown some signs of stabilizing. Over the past three months, employment growth averaged 137,000, compared with an average loss of 45,000 during the same period in 2025. “The core support for consumer spending is being employed,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide financial group. With gas prices trending back down, consumers may begin to see more daylight, she said. Yet wage growth remains stagnant, suggesting employers aren’t yet bidding up the price of job applicants. Meanwhile, the number of Americans who have been out of work for six months or more continues to climb, reaching about 2 million as of the end of October. That group now accounts for 27.6% of all unemployed workers, the highest share since December 2021, a sign of just how tough it can be to find a job. Comments on other recent earnings calls from consumer-facing companies depict a fractured consumer landscape, with some sectors proving resilient and others on shakier ground. The sentiment was echoed by Reynolds Consumer Products, maker of Reynolds Wrap and Hefty. “Household budgets remain under pressure, and we continue to see that reflected in purchasing behavior across our categories,” CEO Scott Huckins said, noting shoppers are more aggressively pursuing promotions and discounts or larger value-pack sizes. Executives with Bloomin’ Brands, the parent company of Outback Steakhouse, were somewhat more upbeat. “What we’re seeing with the consumer is casual dining is still an affordable luxury,” CEO Michael Spanos said on the company’s most recent earnings call. “Consumers, they’re resilient financially, they are cautious, and they continue to be discerning about when, where and how often they dine out.” Even McDonald’s has struggled to draw customers despite offering $5 and $6 meal deals and other promotions. It reported a 0.2% decline in U.S. same-store sales in the third quarter, its first quarterly drop since early last year. “And particularly for that low-income consumer, they’re looking for great entry-level value,” CEO Chris Kempczinski said on the company’s earnings call. “And we have not had that in place to the level that we are satisfied with.”

articles.title: Stake in Singapore arms pledged with lenders: Tata Power
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tata Power said its shareholding in two Singapore subsidiaries targeted by enforcement proceedings in a $650 million arbitration dispute with
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tata Power said its shareholding in two Singapore subsidiaries targeted by enforcement proceedings in a $650 million arbitration dispute with Kleros Capital Partners has already been pledged to lenders, as the Indian utility seeks to prevent any sale of the assets pending an appeal before Singapore's highest court.To sell Tata Power's shares in its Singapore-based subsidiaries, Tata Power International and Bhira Investments, Kleros will first have to deal with the lenders, outgoing MD Praveer Sinha said, adding that the legal process itself could take three to six months.The comments come days after Kleros said enforcement orders obtained from the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) had enabled court-appointed authorities to seize and sell Tata Power's shareholdings in the two entities.The dispute relates to the Krutogorovo coal deposit in Russia's Kamchatka region. Kleros alleged that Tata Power used confidential information obtained under agreements between the parties to pursue the project independently, leading to arbitration proceedings in Singapore. The Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) ruled in 2023 that Tata Power breached non-disclosure agreements with Kleros and, in 2025, awarded the investment firm damages of $490 million, along with interest and costs.Tata Power challenged the awards before the SICC in October 2025, but the court dismissed its applications in August this year. The SICC subsequently passed judgments in September permitting enforcement of the awards. The company has appealed before the Singapore Court of Appeal, with the matter scheduled to be heard on Jan 19, 2027.In a disclosure accompanying its second-quarter results, Tata Power said notices were served on Tata Power International and Bhira Investments on Nov 6 informing them that the company's shareholding in the entities had been attached by court-appointed authorities.Tata Power said it is in the process of filing objections to the enforcement proceedings. If Kleros contests those objections, the company may be required to seek release of the attached shares before the SICC. The sheriff can commence the sale or transfer process only after such an application is decided, and the decision is itself appealable. Tata Power also plans to seek deferment of any sale pending the outcome of its appeal.Tata Power maintained that it continues to retain control over the financial and operating policies of the two subsidiaries and continues to enjoy the economic benefits arising from them.You use AI every day. articles.title: Record FPI buying in November sends sensex to near 9-month high
articles.summary: MUMBAI: After more than two years, foreign funds are back buying Indian stocks.
articles.body: MUMBAI: After more than two years, foreign funds are back buying Indian stocks. In just eight trading sessions in Nov, on a net basis, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have pumped in a little over Rs 73,200 crore into Indian equities, an all-time monthly high figure that surpassed the previous record of Rs 66,135 crore in Dec 2023, data from NSDL and BSE showed.On Wednesday, FPIs net bought stocks worth Rs 12,563 crore. This, combined with the recent crash in crude prices, down about 21% this month, helped Sensex gain another 1% (773 points) to close at 81,879, nearly a nine-month high level.So far in Nov, in eight trading sessions, the bellwether index has gained 10%, about 7,400 points, and investors' wealth has jumped Rs 36 lakh crore to its highest level of Rs 510.7 lakh crore, BSE data showed. During the same period, Nifty has gained 9.7% to its Wednesday close at 25,255 points. Over the last two weeks, several factors have combined to work as tailwinds for indices, market players said.Investors’ wealth up by 4.3L crFor long, Indian companies were seen as laggards in the AI revolution that gripped some of the developed markets. As a result, several foreign fund managers took money off India to invest in AI-related stocks elsewhere. The trend is now reversing, benefitting the Indian market, brokers and analysts said.The recent US midterm poll results, seen as a rebuke to US President Donald Trump’s policies, raised prospects of a diplomatic solution to the war in West Asia, helping cool down crude prices and lower inflation expectations globally, including in India.As a result, the rupee strengthened and is up 1.3% this month to 93.7 to the dollar now. Relatively good corporate results for the July-Sept quarter (Q2FY27) also helped improve investor sentiment significantly.Siddhartha Khemka, head of research - wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said Indian equities are likely to retain their positive momentum, supported by an improving earnings trajectory, a sharp correction in crude prices and a strong resurgence in foreign investors’ flows.“Q2FY27 earnings are increasingly coming in ahead of expectations, strengthening confidence in corporate earnings recovery and providing fundamental support to the ongoing rally.”Cos’ M-cap at 510.7l crIn Wednesday’s session, investors’ wealth went up by about Rs 4.3 lakh crore with the aggregate market value of companies listed on the BSE at Rs 510.7 lakh crore, an all-time high figure, exchange data showed.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Embattled Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair.
articles.body:
Embattled Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair.

The company's board is reportedly meeting to determine if it will oust Huang as chief executive, the Wall Street Journal reports . Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following the report.

According to The New York Times , Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell.

She joined Nvidia in 2008 and heads up the company's healthcare business.

The Times report says that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel during a company conference in March, and that when a bystander took a photo of the interaction, a security guard "sequestered them" and made them an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

Last month, The Times reported that US intelligence services believed a woman, Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, may have acted as an intelligence asset , sharing information with the ruling party in Beijing.

On Sunday, Huang issued a statement apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees for having an affair, though he didn't name with whom.

In response, Nvidia's board said it is launching an independent investigation into the matter.

"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board said in a statement Sunday.

articles.body:
Shares of Nvidia tanked early Wednesday evening, after The New York Times reported that CEO Jensen Huang had a second affair .

The company’s stock was down roughly 8.3 percent during after hours trading, dipping below $160 per share. Nvidia shares had not fallen below that threshold since June 2025.

Nvidia shares were trading at greater than $200 as recently as a week ago, and reached an all-time high of $243.37 on Oct. 6.

But the company’s stock has dropped since the NYT reported Huang had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang , whom U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. Alice Huang has worked for Megaspeed , a Singaporean firm that is a customer of Nvidia.

Then on Wednesday, the paper reported on a second affair Jensen Huang had with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care.

The NYT cited five people who worked at the tech giant, whose chips power the AI industry. Jensen Huang has led Nvidia since he founded the company in 1993.

The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday evening that the company’s board, which brought in former federal prosecutor Joon H. Kim to lead an investigation into Huang, was preparing to oust the CEO.

The Hill has reached out to Nvidia for comment. The Journal reported the board is preparing to meet as soon as today regarding Jensen Huang’s future.

Jensen Huang, an ally of President Trump, acknowledged he had an affair, saying in a company memo he was “unfaithful” to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang, Bloomberg reported Sunday.

Democrats and Republicans on Capitol Hill have cited Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang as justification for restricting exports of Nvidia’s chips.

But Trump has stood by the Nvidia CEO, calling Jensen Huang an “honorable guy” on Sunday.

“I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on,” the president told reporters.

articles.title: Nvidia Working With Outside Firm to Identify CEO Candidates
articles.summary: Nvidia Corp.’s board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following reports of m...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Nvidia Corp.'s board has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who is reportedly suspected of spying for China, a person familiar with the situation said.

The board is weighing the idea of naming a temporary chief while searching for a permanent one, the person said, asking not to be identified because the information isn't public. Directors were meeting on Wednesday to discuss Huang's fate, according to people familiar with the situation. The Wall Street Journal said earlier that the board was preparing to oust Huang, citing unidentified people familiar with the matter. Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Nvidia's board has been facing a succession crisis since Sunday when Huang admitted that he'd had an affair with Alice Huang, a data center executive at a company that is one of Nvidia's largest Southeast Asian customers. The New York Times has reported that Alice Huang was suspected of operating as an agent on behalf of the Chinese government.

The crisis escalated late Wednesday, when the Times reported that Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, citing unidentified people who worked at the company. Powell didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The disclosure and subsequent reports have left the board with a difficult option: ousting the founder and only person ever to have run Nvidia, firing an executive who — at least until recently — had commanded widespread respect of shareholders and customers alike and oversaw a more than 700,000% surge in the company's share price.

But keeping Jensen Huang in the role would likely subject Nvidia to a barrage of scrutiny from lawmakers, investors, customers and staff concerned over his relationship with Alice Huang and whether it put Nvidia's trade secrets at risk — as well as his extramarital relationship with a person who directly reported to him at the company.

The developments have also shined a light on Nvidia's lack of a succession plan for Huang, and reinforced how inseparable the 63-year-old CEO is from the company and its success. His potential exit would reverberate far beyond the company's operations, and not just because Nvidia is the dominant maker of chips at the heart of the AI boom.

articles.title: Nvidia shares plunge amid reports board to discuss CEO Huang’s future
articles.summary: Chip giant’s stock price falls more than 8 percent amid speculation over co-founder’s position.
articles.body:
Chip giant Nvidia’s stock price has tumbled amid reports that its board of directors is meeting to consider the future of CEO Jensen Huang.

Nvidia shares fell 8.6 percent in after-hours trading on Wednesday as questions swirled over Huang’s position at the top of the $4.2 trillion company.

The plunge comes after The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times reported that Nvidia’s board of directors would discuss Huang’s position over allegations that he engaged in an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, in addition to an affair with a woman accused of working with Chinese intelligence services.

Nvidia, which launched an investigation into Huang on Sunday, did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, is one of the most visible faces of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, spearheading the development of high-end graphics processing units used to train and run frontier models.

The leather jacket-sporting tech executive’s position has also placed him at the centre of the geopolitical rivalry between the United States and China, which are locked in a battle for supremacy in AI.

As a confidant of US President Donald Trump, Huang has lobbied for the easing of restrictions on exports of high-end chips to China, putting him at odds with national security hawks in Washington who argue that Beijing must be blocked from access to cutting-edge US tech.

If Nvidia’s board were to oust Huang, 63, it would mark a seismic moment for the chip giant.

Viewed as integral to Nvidia’s meteoric rise to the ranks of the world’s most valuable companies, Huang is known for a centralised leadership style that places him at the centre of the company’s day-to-day operations and strategic decisions.

“Jensen is Nvidia; without him, the company loses its central, animating spirit,” Jay Goldberg, a senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, told Al Jazeera.

“The organisation is built around him and replacing him will be very painful organisationally, and impossible to do personality-wise.”

It is unclear whether Nvidia has a succession plan, and analysts see few obvious candidates to take Huang’s place.

Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said Huang has been the “hearts and lungs” of Nvidia and that investors will closely scrutinise the executive’s possible replacement.

“We believe Nvidia’s value is $300 per share with Jensen as CEO and $225 per share without Jensen as CEO,” Ives said in a note to clients, adding that the company would navigate the turmoil and “remain a core foundational piece of the AI Revolution.”

“Jensen is not replaceable by another CEO or group of interim executives, but Nvidia likely now has to move on without Jensen at the helm, which seemed like a Twilight Zone episode narrative before Sunday afternoon when the news broke,” Ives said.

Nvidia has been the focus of international intrigue over the past week amid reports that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese woman who US intelligence officials determined had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security.

US officials have not provided evidence for the claims about the woman, a Chinese tech executive named Alice Huang.

Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, has not publicly commented on the allegations.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied the claims, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.

Nvidia’s board of directors said on Sunday it had opened a probe into whether Huang had been targeted in a foreign intelligence operation, while also expressing confidence in the executive.

Huang, who admitted to being “unfaithful” to his wife and apologised to his family, pledged to cooperate fully with the inquiry and said he was committed to protecting Nvidia and US national security.

Negotiators from Moscow and Kyiv agreed to a major prisoner exchange following two days of US-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi, which concluded on Wednesday. However, disagreements over key issues, particularly territorial control, remain unresolved. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has said Kyiv hopes to make tangible progress towards ending the war this year.The possibility of the Iran conflict avoiding further escalation ahead of next week's US-China summit has also influenced market sentiment."Markets are falling on expectations that behind-the-scenes efforts are underway to secure a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine and that it is unlikely the Iran war will escalate ahead of the US-China summit next week," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities.He said the situation around the Strait of Hormuz could nevertheless prevent a steep decline in crude prices."However, given the uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, the markets are unlikely to suffer a significant collapse," Kikukawa said.Tensions over Iran's nuclear programme continue to complicate the prospect of negotiations. articles.title: Nvidia Turmoil Lifts AMD, Broadcom on Bets for Business Gains
articles.summary: Nvidia Corp.’s leadership turmoil is boosting potential beneficiaries, with Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Broadcom Inc. and Alphabet Inc. gaining after hours...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Nvidia Corp.'s leadership turmoil is boosting potential beneficiaries, with Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Broadcom Inc. and Alphabet Inc. gaining after hours on bets they may win business from the chip giant.

AMD and Broadcom each rose more than 3% as Nvidia sank 9% after hours on reports its board is preparing to oust Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, who led its rise to become, at one point, the world's most valuable company. Alphabet rose 0.3% in extended trading.

The selloff followed reports about Huang's extramarital affairs and intensified after the Wall Street Journal said the board was preparing to remove him. Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Huang.

As Nvidia confronts leadership uncertainty, rival hardware makers are gaining as investors seek continued exposure to the AI trade while hedging Nvidia-related risks. The turmoil underscores the potential for further volatility as investors assess its impact on AI development and the extent to which customers diversify their spending worldwide.

"This is where competitors like AMD, like Google Tensor Processing Units and Amazon will probably have a chance to improve their market share when it comes to that accelerator market that Nvidia dominates," Mandeep Singh, global head of technology research at Bloomberg Intelligence, said. "There is no doubt that Nvidia won't be as aggressive as they have been in the past two to three years when it comes to setting goals and overachieving them."

Huang's potential replacement will likely be "quite conservative" in company leadership, given the recent developments.

AMD and Broadcom stand to likely gain the most if Nvidia's leadership issues disrupt its customer relationships. AMD is Nvidia's closest rival in AI accelerators, while Broadcom has a growing role in custom AI chips and networking.

While a Nvidia leadership shakeup may push customers to rethink their reliance on a single supplier, competitors like AMD and Broadcom are already pursuing business in AI accelerators, custom silicon and networking.

"AMD as a direct competitor, and Alphabet and Broadcom in the TPU space, are natural beneficiaries in the short term," said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. "Huang's scandal has raised public doubts about Nvidia's commercial secrets and its product edge."

articles.title: Son faced tax notices over Rs 20.23 lakh property purchase and Rs 13.04 lakh cash deposits; ITAT accepts mother's gold-sale gift deed evidence and deletes addition
articles.summary: You buy a property and also deposit cash in your bank account.
articles.body: You buy a property and also deposit cash in your bank account. The Income Tax department treats both as unexplained income and asks you to file your income tax return. What do you do?A resident of Jaipur attracted the Income Tax Department's attention after purchasing a property and depositing cash in his bank account without filing an income tax return.What the case is aboutA man purchased a property worth Rs 20.23 lakh and deposited Rs 13.04 lakh in cash into his bank account. The department had received information about these transactions and began proceedings to investigate the source of the funds used for the investment and cash deposits.During the proceedings, the taxpayer filed his income tax return, declaring an income of Rs 2,14,997. However, the Assessing Officer (AO) treated both the property investment of Rs 20,23,778 and the cash deposits of Rs 13,04,900 as unexplained. This resulted in additions of Rs 33,28,678, or approximately Rs 33.29 lakh, to the man’s income.The person contested the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals). The appellate authority removed the addition relating to the property purchase but retained the Rs 13,04,900 addition for unexplained cash deposits.He subsequently approached the Jaipur Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), challenging the amount that continued to be treated as unexplained income.In an order dated October 6, 2026, ITAT Jaipur decided the matter in the man’s favour and deleted the addition of Rs 13,04,900 relating to the cash deposits. The addition concerning the property investment had already been removed by the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).Why did ITAT rule in favour of the assessee?The person’s counsel told ITAT Jaipur the assessee’s mother had sold her old gold jewellery and given her son Rs 16 lakh in cash. A registered valuer had assessed the jewellery's value at Rs 18,36,230 in 2011.The Assessing Officer was not satisfied with this explanation because the documents relating to the jewellery sale did not list the individual gold items. The cousel countered that old jewellery is commonly sold in the trade on the basis of its aggregate weight, without each item being separately described on the invoice.The AO had also raised questions about the difference between the total weight recorded in the valuation report and the quantity of jewellery sold. Responding to this objection, the counsel submitted that the person’s mother had sold 642.300 grams of jewellery for Rs 16,10,567 and subsequently gifted Rs 16 lakh to her son.To support the explanation, the person relied on a notarised gift deed bearing the signatures of two witnesses and the valuation report prepared by the registered valuer. The tribunal also noted that the man had deposited a total of Rs 16,05,000 into his bank account between February 4 and March 31, 2012.After examining the arguments and supporting documents, ITAT Jaipur accepted the man’s explanation for the source of the cash deposits.The tribunal observed: “This gift is from the mother only which is within the relatives as defined in Section 2(41). Further the assesee’s mother in her old age gifted part of the amount from sale of her gold jewellery given as gift to the assessee, which cannot be doubted, since the same is supported by valid notarised Gift Deed with two witnesses and value of the jewels were determined by Registered Valuer. Thus the addition made by the AO is liable to be deleted.”On this basis, the tribunal removed the addition of Rs 13,04,900 that had been made for unexplained cash deposits.Chartered Accountant Varun Singhal told ET that taxpayers seeking to explain the source of funds through a gift should take certain precautions. They should establish where the donor obtained the money instead of relying only on documentation confirming that the gift was made. It is also important to retain documents created at the relevant time, such as the gift deed, valuation report and jewellery-sale invoice.Taxpayers should maintain a clear documentary trail connecting the gift to the subsequent bank deposits, ensuring that the dates and amounts can be matched. Where available, the donor's bank statements and other financial records should also be preserved.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: MUMBAI: Tata Investment Corporation has appointed Bahram Vakil as chairman, completing a boardroom handover that has seen Noel Tata step down from a
articles.body: MUMBAI: Tata Investment Corporation has appointed Bahram Vakil as chairman, completing a boardroom handover that has seen Noel Tata step down from a string of Tata companies on reaching the group’s retirement age.The appointment is the second in quick succession for Vakil. He had already been named chairman of Trent, the group’s retail arm behind Westside and Zudio, on the same timetable, succeeding Noel.The reshuffle extends beyond Tata Investment and Trent. At Tata International, T V Narendran, chief executive and managing director of Tata Steel, will become chairman, succeeding Noel Tata. Narendran, already a non-executive director on the Tata International board, takes over as part of the same retirement-driven change.Vakil, co-founder of law firm AZB & Partners, takes over from Nov 12, a day after Noel Tata retired as chairman and director at the close of business on November 11. Noel, who joined the board in June 2004 and had chaired the company since June 2010, becomes chairman emeritus.For a group long defined by family stewardship and Tata lifers, the appointment is notable. Vakil is a corporate lawyer, not an operating executive. He is, however, no stranger to the group. He became vice-chairman and independent director of Tata Investment in March 2025, giving him a front-row seat before his elevation.There is also precedent for turning to an outsider. In 2005, Ratan Tata stepped down as chairman of VSNL, now Tata Communications and independent director Subodh Bhargava took over. In 2017, private equity veteran Renuka Ramnath became chairperson of Tata Communications, succeeding Bhargava.Under Tata Group guidelines, non-executive, non-independent directors retire at 70. Noel turns 70 on Nov 12. He will remain chairman of Tata Trusts and a Tata Trusts nominee on the board of Tata Sons, the holding company. Narendran's appointment keeps Tata International, the group’s trading and distribution arm, under a Tata operating chief, in contrast to Tata Investment and Trent, where the chairmanship has passed to an outside professional. articles.summary: Nvidia's board is reportedly weighing the future of CEO Jensen Huang, turning the attention to who could take charge of the world's most valuable
articles.body: Nvidia's board is reportedly weighing the future of CEO Jensen Huang, turning the attention to who could take charge of the world's most valuable chipmaker if the 63-year-old executive is forced out or decides to step down.Two names have emerged as potential internal successors: Ian Buck, a veteran engineer who helped develop Nvidia's CUDA software platform, and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who has been with the company for more than a decade, reported Reuters, citing internal sources. While Buck is seen as a possible long-term choice because of his technical expertise, Kress is being viewed as a candidate who could provide continuity in the immediate term.Nvidia's board was meeting on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Huang, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters. Separately, reports by Bloomberg and Semafor have indicated that the board is considering an interim chief while it looks for a permanent replacement, with some board members favouring Kress for the temporary role.Huang has never named a successor. The board is also said to be working with an external firm to identify potential candidates, with possibilities ranging from senior Nvidia executives to leaders outside the company.Colette Kress or Ian Buck?Kress, 59, is reportedly among the most prominent internal candidates for an interim appointment. She joined Nvidia in 2013 after holding senior finance positions at Microsoft, Cisco and Texas Instruments. As CFO, she regularly appears alongside Huang on the company's quarterly earnings calls, making her a familiar face to investors."Colette Kress is the obvious choice to steady the ship. She has been CFO for 13 years and fronts every earnings call alongside him, so she’s a familiar and trusted voice for the market at a time when it badly needs one," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst at trading platform eToro.However, the permanent leadership role could call for someone with a stronger technical background, particularly given Nvidia's position in the artificial intelligence industry. "The permanent job is a different story, though, because Nvidia’s edge comes from its technology, and the board would likely want an engineer in the chair. Someone like Ian Buck, who led the software platform that keeps developers tied to Nvidia’s chips, is the sort of internal name you’d expect to come up," Gilbert added, as quoted by Reuters.Buck, now in his late 40s, joined Nvidia in 2004 and played a key role in developing CUDA, the software platform that has helped make the company's chips central to AI development. He currently manages Nvidia's AI hardware and software products as head of product for hyperscale AI.A Stanford PhD, Buck has also been involved in Nvidia's efforts to expand its AI computing capabilities. "If a transition becomes necessary then Ian Buck is the strongest long-term internal candidate given his role in creating CUDA and leading Nvidia’s hyperscale business," said Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities.External candidates and other possibilitiesThe search may not be limited to Nvidia's existing leadership. Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, has also been mentioned as a possible external candidate. Jeff Fisher, a 32-year Nvidia veteran, is another name being reportedly discussed. Huang's two children, who are both executives at the company, have also mentioned in speculation about possible successors.A banker working on semiconductor deals told Reuters that Haas made the most "logical sense" because of his profile and understanding of the chip industry.Boloor also identified Haas as an external candidate worth considering. However, appointing someone from outside Nvidia could present challenges given the company's scale and the specialised nature of its business.Some investors believe the board could opt for a shared leadership arrangement, at least during the transition. "The more realistic route is an interim leader from the long-serving inner circle, possibly as a co-CEO structure: one leader to steady the business and the finances, such as Colette Kress, alongside a product and technology leader, such as Ian Buck," said Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder at Minotaur Capital, which owns Nvidia shares.The succession debate comes as Nvidia faces scrutiny over reports of two alleged extramarital relationships involving Huang. He acknowledged in a letter to employees on Sunday, admitting he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologising for violating their trust.The latest allegations include a reported relationship with Nvidia vice president Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to Huang. The New York Times, citing five people who worked at the company, reported that the relationship had not been previously disclosed. The reports have also raised questions about the company's workplace policies on conflicts of interest and personal relationships.The controversy has added to pressure on Nvidia shares. The stock lost around $430 billion in market value over Monday and Tuesday, falling a combined 9.5%. It recovered 2.9% during Wednesday's regular trading session before dropping more than 8% in after-hours trading following reports that the board was preparing to discuss Huang's future.Huang's leadership has been closely associated with the company's rise, making the prospect of a succession particularly significant for investors. "Jensen Huang is a rockstar in the industry. He’s outspoken and synonymous with the Nvidia brand, and a leader like that is very hard to replace," said Anna Wu, founder of Floodlines Research in Sydney.Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management, also pointed to the scale of Huang's contribution. articles.body:
SINGAPORE, Nov 12 (Reuters) - Global stocks tumbled on Thursday, led by losses in chipmakers and data centre operators as Nvidia shares cratered in after-hours trading on news that its board may oust longtime CEO Jensen Huang.

An 8.8% ‌plunge in Nvidia shares in extended trading reverberated across Asian markets, weighing on S&P 500 e-mini futures, down 0.5%, and triggering ‌broad losses in chip stocks.

Taiwan's benchmark index tumbled 2.6% and South Korea's Kospi fell 0.9%, dragging the MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index down 1.2%. Japan's Nikkei 225 sank 0.9%.

"Nvidia sits ​at the centre of an increasingly interconnected AI ecosystem," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore. "Its turmoil comes when financing, hyperscaler capex, valuations and returns on AI investment were already under scrutiny."

Nvidia's board reportedly met late Wednesday to decide whether to oust Huang, a source familiar with the matter said, as the world's dominant supplier of AI processors grappled with the fallout of allegations that he had an affair with a ‌suspected spy for China. The New York Times has ⁠also reported that Huang had had an affair with a company executive who reported to him.

"It looks bad from every single angle," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer at Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. "I believe the ⁠board won't oust him until they have an all-star, a known entity in the tech sector, to replace him," he said. "At the end of the day, let's not forget that the Nvidia chip is the centrepiece of the AI story."

It's not yet clear who might replace Huang as CEO. In the meantime, Chinese domestic ​GPU ​makers surged on Thursday as expectations rose that Nvidia's troubles could help local ​chip suppliers win greater market share. Chinese AI firms are ‌reportedly rushing to secure Nvidia chip capacity, fearing that the US could cut them off in the wake of the scandal.

Stocks on Wall Street made gains on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 rising 1.3% and coming close to retracing all of the losses since last week's US midterm elections, as CoreWeave reassured investors over its path to profitability by the first half of 2028, lifting semiconductor stocks. The data centre operator gave back some of those gains in after-hours trading, down as much as 3% in Asia on Thursday.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against ‌a basket of six currencies, was up 0.1% at 102.98, its highest level ​since April 9 last year in the aftermath of Trump's Liberation Day tariff announcement. ​The currency has gained 1.3% over the past three sessions as traders ​repriced the odds the Federal Reserve will lift interest rates next month.

articles.title: Why Anthropic's IPO could follow the SpaceX playbook, and what it means for investors
articles.summary: When AI company Anthropic begins trading after its expected IPO next week, its share price in the initial weeks may depend as much on who is required to
articles.body: When AI company Anthropic begins trading after its expected IPO next week, its share price in the initial weeks may depend as much on who is required to buy the stock as on who wants to own it.Investors are looking to Elon Musk's SpaceX, which went public in June, for clues. Its listing changed the playbook for mega-IPOs by triggering rapid inclusion in major stock market indexes, creating a large pool of buyers soon after trading began.Anthropic is expected to follow a similar path. The Claude chatbot maker aims to raise up to $64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares at $70-$78 apiece, valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion.How index inclusion drives demandIndex providers track groups of stocks representing a particular market. Funds that follow these indexes, known as passive funds, must buy shares of companies added to their benchmarks to match the index.Earlier, major providers generally waited weeks or months after an IPO before including a company. But following SpaceX's listing, the rules changed, allowing large companies to enter key indexes much sooner.Anthropic is expected to join at least six major indexes, including FTSE's USA index, the S&P Total Market Index and the Nasdaq 100, within five to 15 days of listing. "Anthropic is a mirror image of the SpaceX IPO. In that regard, it has the same index-related drivers over the first 15 days of trading," said Carsten Hesse, head of index events at Berenberg, as quoted by Reuters.Index analytics firm Intropic estimates that demand from passive funds could account for around 28% of Anthropic's shares on offer, or roughly $19 billion.Funds tracking an index typically buy shares when the inclusion takes effect. But hedge funds and specialist traders often buy earlier, anticipating this demand and hoping to profit from a rise in the share price.The relatively small public float could amplify this effect. Only around 6% of Anthropic's outstanding shares are being offered in the IPO.SpaceX followed a similar pattern. It reserved a fifth of its $75 billion offering for retail investors, more than twice the usual allocation. Retail investors and index funds bought nearly half the shares sold, while other fund managers positioned themselves for further demand.SpaceX shares rose 50% from their opening-day debut price by the third day of trading and remained above the IPO price for the first 15 days. "You don't wait till day 5, day 10, day 15, when you see the implementation of the index upgrades or inclusions," Hesse said. "As we've seen with SpaceX, people are buying early."What could be different this time?The start of options trading can also add to early buying. When traders take positions in stock options, they may buy or sell the underlying shares to hedge their exposure. SpaceX and South Korean firm SK Hynix both saw sharp gains on the third day of trading, when options trading began.Anthropic's trajectory could differ, however. Employees, who own around 15 per cent of its equity, will be allowed to sell some shares on the first day. The company is also raising $26 billion through a separate private sale involving investors such as Google, Nvidia and AMD. Those shares will not have a lock-up period, which normally restricts early investors from selling for a specified time.The faster index inclusion of mega-IPOs has created bigger opportunities for funds that trade around index changes. Such investors buy shares ahead of passive funds, hoping to benefit when the latter enter the market.Earlier, these trades were limited by smaller IPO sizes and the risk of too many investors chasing the same opportunity. Mega-listings offer a much larger pool of shares and potential demand. "It's a bit of an evolution of the market," said Brian Hartigan, global head of ETFs and index investments at Invesco."If you're in index rebalancing, these are probably the events of a lifetime," said Bill Park, CIO of Altisma Capital Management.You use AI every day. articles.title: As gold falls from Rs 1.8 lakh peak to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, Indians buy 30% more, spending Rs 72,000 crore on 52 tonnes; silver demand rises 10%
articles.summary: Gold prices falling from their record highs has led to Indian consumers increasing their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period.
articles.body: Gold prices falling from their record highs has led to Indian consumers increasing their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.The industry body estimated that consumers purchased 52 tonnes of gold worth Rs 72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at Rs 5,400 crore during this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations.Gold price correction from Rs 1.8 lakh peakThe increase followed a correction in gold prices from a peak of around Rs 1.8 lakh to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, drawing buyers back into the market. Purchases made in advance of the wedding season, which starts in mid-November and runs until March, also helped boost demand.“Jewellers have made good business in this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali,” IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET.Mehta said the market was witnessing pent-up demand, as several consumers had put off buying gold after Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to people not to purchase the metal.“Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing .”The festival calendar also worked in favour of jewellery purchases. Dhanteras was observed on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8. Both occasions fell in the early part of the month, when salaried employees typically receive their monthly pay and festive bonuses.“This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment,” said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council.In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%. The fall was attributed to higher prices, an increase in import duty and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal to consumers to refrain from buying gold.Gold generates big returnsDespite the volatility, gold has generated significant returns over the past few years. Prices, which were around Rs 60,000 per 10 grams in 2023, climbed to Rs 80,000 in 2024 and reached Rs 1.15 lakh-Rs 1.20 lakh in 2025. During this year’s Dhanteras-Diwali period, prices stood at approximately Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver has also recorded a substantial appreciation in value.An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers found that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third-highest in a decade, even though prices were around 10% above their level a year earlier.“The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period,” said C Vinod Hayagriv, director of C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers.Natural diamonds also held up well, registering their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer recorded a 250% increase in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras, while sales during the Diwali season rose 47%.The performance comes at a time when the natural diamond industry is facing disruption from global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and increasing competition from lab-grown alternatives. articles.title: Niño Becerra lanza una advertencia sobre el posible futuro de las pensiones en España: "Sigan el desarrollo de este asunto"
articles.standfirst: El economista ha publicado en sus redes sociales una escueta referencia al banco paraguayo intervenido
articles.summary: El economista ha publicado en sus redes sociales una escueta referencia al banco paraguayo intervenido
articles.body: Santiago Niño Becerra ha publicado un mensaje tan breve como enigmático en sus redes sociales. El economista se ha limitado a escribir "Ueno Bank de Paraguay" y añadir una recomendación: "Sigan el desarrollo de este asunto". Sin ofrecer más explicaciones ni establecer ninguna conexión explícita, el catedrático de Economía ha puesto el foco en una entidad financiera cuya intervención ha provocado una importante crisis en Paraguay y ha dejado en una situación de incertidumbre a miles de ahorradores y a distintos fondos con recursos destinados a jubilaciones. La publicación llega, además, en un momento en el que el futuro del sistema público de pensiones se ha situado en el centro del debate político en España. En las últimas semanas, el diputado de Vox José María Figaredo ha defendido la necesidad de avanzar hacia un modelo mixto que combine el sistema de reparto actual con la capitalización individual. Aunque Niño Becerra no menciona las pensiones españolas ni a ningún partido político, su referencia al caso paraguayo puede interpretarse como una advertencia sobre los riesgos que entraña la exposición de los ahorros destinados a la jubilación a entidades financieras. El Banco Central de Paraguay inició el 3 de noviembre el procedimiento de resolución de Ueno Bank después de detectar que su índice de solvencia había caído por debajo del 50% del mínimo exigido. La decisión llegó tras una revisión de sus estados financieros en la que se identificaron problemas en la calidad de sus activos, operaciones crediticias con empresas vinculadas a su grupo controlador que no habían sido reveladas oportunamente y deficiencias en la documentación de determinadas operaciones. La intervención supuso la suspensión de las operaciones de la entidad y dejó temporalmente sin acceso a sus cuentas a millones de clientes. Ueno Bank se había convertido en uno de los bancos más populares del país, con alrededor de 2,9 millones de clientes, según los datos difundidos por la agencia EFE. El caso adquirió también una dimensión política por los vínculos empresariales que se atribuyeron al presidente paraguayo, Santiago Peña, con el grupo económico relacionado con la entidad. Reuters informó de que las autoridades investigaban posibles responsabilidades y de que la crisis había generado una fuerte controversia institucional. Pero uno de los aspectos que más preocupación ha despertado es la cantidad de recursos públicos y fondos vinculados a jubilaciones que estaban depositados o invertidos en productos relacionados con el banco. Según la información publicada por EFE, distintas instituciones estatales tenían alrededor de 800 millones de dólares en la entidad, una parte importante de ellos procedentes de recursos relacionados con pensiones. Entre los casos que han salido a la luz está el de la Entidad Binacional Yacyretá. Un fondo complementario de jubilaciones de sus trabajadores había invertido 10 millones de dólares en certificados de depósito de ahorro de Ueno Bank, con un interés anual del 6,9% y vencimiento previsto para mayo de 2027. La entidad ha anunciado acciones para intentar recuperar el capital y los intereses. Yacyretá ha precisado que esos recursos pertenecen a un fideicomiso de adhesión voluntaria de sus trabajadores y que no forman parte de su patrimonio institucional ni constituyen una caja de jubilaciones. Es una distinción importante para entender el alcance real del problema. El caso paraguayo coincide con el debate abierto en España sobre una posible transformación del sistema público de pensiones. El pasado octubre, José María Figaredo defendió en una entrevista la necesidad de una reforma estructural porque, en sus palabras, el sistema actual "lo han quebrado". El diputado de Vox propuso avanzar hacia un modelo mixto que combine el reparto con la capitalización individual. La diferencia entre ambos sistemas es relevante. En el modelo de reparto, las cotizaciones de los trabajadores en activo financian las prestaciones de los pensionistas actuales. En uno de capitalización, las aportaciones se acumulan e invierten para financiar la futura jubilación de cada persona. Un modelo mixto combina ambos mecanismos, aunque su funcionamiento depende de cómo se diseñe y de quién gestione los fondos. Figaredo ha defendido esa fórmula, aunque posteriormente negó que su partido pretendiera privatizar las pensiones. El programa económico de Vox de 2025 sí recoge la intención de iniciar la capitalización de un fondo público de pensiones con criterios de rentabilidad privada y avanzar hacia un sistema mixto, aunque no concreta todos los detalles de su aplicación.
